PeopleModels - posed human figures for the night jewellery-store scene
Prepared October 14-15, 2026; examiner white levels revised October 15, 2026; LOD variants of two
figures added October 15, 2026.
Not yet imported or checked in Unity.

Seven static figures (OBJ/MTL plus textures) made from five avatars of the Microsoft Rocketbox
Avatar Library, posed with one frame of a Rocketbox motion-capture animation and baked to a
static mesh. Small hand props (notebook, pen, phone, camera) and their texture atlas are
project-made. Exact source paths, the upstream commit and SHA-256 hashes of every source file
and every shipped file are in sources.json.

Avatars and animations used (paths in the repository):

  Assets/Avatars/Professions/Medical_Male_04    (textures m162_*)  -> ForensicExaminer_*

     m_take_picture (frame 80), m_idle_look_around_02 (frame 40),
     m_cell_phone_textmessage (frame 100), f_documents_note (frame 150)

What was changed (all scripts are in Source~):
  - Geometry: the hipoly skinned mesh of each avatar was posed with one animation frame
    (body bones copied in world space, Blender 5.2.2 as the bpy module), evaluated and baked to a
    static OBJ in metres, Y up, facing +Z, feet on y = 0, centred in x/z. No rig, no blend
    shapes. Material names were renamed to Body/Head/Equipment/Pistol/Protection/Hair.
    DetectiveFemale hair cards are duplicated back-to-back so they render from both sides with
    back-face culling.
  - Textures: 2048 px TGA converted to JPG (colour 2048 px, normal 1024 px; Equipment and
    Pistol smaller) and the Rocketbox specular map packed into a metallic/smoothness PNG.
    PoliceOfficer_Equipment: the small "RBX" badge on the radio was cloned out.
    PoliceOfficer_Pistol: two maker-style grip medallions were cloned out.
    ForensicExaminer_Body: the green medical scrubs were recoloured to a white disposable
    coverall with long sleeves and the hands to blue nitrile gloves (texture edit, the mesh is
    unchanged). ForensicExaminer_Protection: the surgical cap was recoloured white.
    Revision October 15, 2026: the white of both maps was lowered to a median of 220 sRGB with
    the highlights rolled off, so that no texel exceeds 240 (it was near-clipped at 245-255
    before). The glove highlights roll off the same way, the cuffs blend over two texels, the
    unused UV space is edge-padded, and the JPGs are saved 4:4:4 with a check that no decoded
    texel exceeds 240 (this also caps the mask's few brightest texels, 241-243, at 240).
    The sleeve/body labelling is now deterministic, which also changed the Body normal map
    slightly (two triangles at the right shoulder now count as sleeve).
    DetectiveFemale_Hair_Color.png keeps the RGBA hair/eyelash atlas (1024 x 512) with the
    colour bled into transparent texels.
  - LOD variants (October 15, 2026): PasserBy_Phone_LOD1.obj and PasserBy_Phone_LOD2.obj were
    decimated from PasserBy_Phone.obj, and PoliceOfficer_Standing_LOD1.obj and
    PoliceOfficer_Standing_LOD2.obj from PoliceOfficer_Standing.obj, by Source~/make_lods.py
    (seam-aware half-edge collapse: every vertex is an original vertex of the source and every
    corner an original UV/normal pair of the same material). They use the original MTL files and
    textures. The hand-prop groups of the passer-by (Props, PropScreen) are copied unchanged.
  - The modified files remain under the MIT License (same copyright notice).

  PoliceOfficer_Standing_LOD1.obj, PoliceOfficer_Standing_LOD2.obj (decimated from
  PoliceOfficer_Standing.obj).

Content notes: the avatars are generic characters made by the Rocketbox artists, not likenesses
of named people. Uniform text is the generic word "POLICE"; the detective's small belt badge reads
"LIEUTENANT A. SMITH ... DEPARTMENT POLICE" (generic, no real agency name or seal). No product
brands or logos remain after the edits above.

This pack is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft.

2. Project-owned original work
===============================================================================
Author:   Jewelry-store-vr-demo project (made with Claude, October 2026). No third-party input.
Licence:  Project-owned; may be used, modified and redistributed with the project.
Files:    PeopleProps_Color.jpg, PeopleProps_MetallicSmoothness.png (procedural atlas: notebook
          cover and handwritten-style page with illegible scribble lines, pen, phone body and a
          blurred generic camera-app screen with a recording timer, camera body, lens, flash), the hand-prop geometry inside the
          OBJ files, including the LOD variants (groups Props and PropScreen: pocket notebook and
          ballpoint pen, smartphone, DSLR with zoom lens and speedlight), and everything in Source~
          (build scripts, among them make_lods.py, copied from the project's StreetModels pack, and
          Preview.jpg, a Blender Cycles render of the seven figures, not a Unity screenshot).
          No real product shapes, names or logos.
